title: From URL to pixels
outcome: Trace navigation, browser work, and the boundary between server and client.
version: Portable JavaScript · React hooks · Vue 2/3 comparisons · Next App Router

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: A client route works after clicking but returns a server 404 on refresh. Explain the missing boundary.

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: A clock renders one time on the server and a later time on the first client render. How do you avoid a hydration mismatch?

trace.title: URL request
trace.detail: The browser turns a URL into a request, receives HTML, builds a DOM tree, loads CSS and JavaScript, and paints pixels. JavaScript can change the DOM later. Layout calculates geometry. Paint draws visible styles. These are different costs.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
Trace document request → HTML parsing → CSS/layout → script → UI change. Then trace a client navigation separately. The network requests and work can differ.

For a slow page, determine whether the wait is server response time, asset loading, script execution, layout, or a later API call. A single “loading” label hides several possible causes.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: A new Date() or random value rendered independently on server and client can produce different first markup. Browser-only APIs such as localStorage are not available during server execution.
